caseStudyPage.approachHeading: Turning complexity into work the team could own.

centerbase.title: Turning accounting reports from a wait into an answer.
centerbase.summary: Centerbase is a multi-tenant legal-operations SaaS used by hundreds of US law firms. I led a reporting redesign for its hardest domain—accounting—so customers and their accounting teams could move from a frustrating wait of tens of seconds to results in about one second.
centerbase.team: ~40 delivery team · Dev Lead across 3 initiatives

metrics.label: report response, down from tens of seconds

challenge.title: The reporting layer had to unify a complex financial domain—at runtime.
challenge.body: Core accounting had more than 20 transaction types, with data spread across many MS SQL tables. Chart of Accounts, Health Check, and T-Account reports called a stored procedure over a view with 98 SELECT branches joined by UNION ALL. Every report rebuilt that data model before a customer could see an answer.

approach.title: Mapped every report branch to its source transaction
approach.body: I traced each SELECT branch in the original view to the stored procedure and source table that produced its transaction type. That gave the redesign an explicit, testable mapping instead of an inferred reporting query.

approach.title: Prepared reporting data as transactions were created
approach.body: I designed and implemented a flat mapping table. Immediately after each original transaction insert, a dedicated stored procedure synchronously inserted its corresponding reporting record into that table.

approach.title: Replaced the expensive read path
approach.body: The reports moved from the 98-branch view to a lightweight SELECT against the prepared mapping table, filtered by transaction type. The new path ran correctly in production and replaced the former reporting view.

outcome.title: Accounting teams could get the answer while the question still mattered.
outcome.body: The new reporting path improved performance by 300%: reports that had made users wait tens of seconds now typically return in about one second. Customers and accounting teams responded positively because they could look up information immediately.
points: Implemented the core solution directly, from source analysis through production rollout.
Gave future reporting features a clear mapping model across 20+ transaction types.
Kept accounting detail accurate without rebuilding the entire view on every request.

supportingCases.title: A document service that brought the legal workflow into Word and Outlook.
supportingCases.body: As Dev Lead, I worked with a distributed team of 4 developers in Vietnam and 1–2 in the US to build an independently deployable document service. It used Microsoft Graph and SharePoint while the add-ins called Core APIs for the business context they needed.
highlights: A right-side panel surfaced matters, billing entries, and document templates directly inside Word and Outlook.
Selected template data could be inserted into content or generated as a table, keeping document work close to the customer conversation.
Each active tab had its own timer ID, persisted in storage and the database so time tracking followed the active document context.

supportingCases.title: A central payment gateway, separated from the monolith.
supportingCases.body: I designed new modules and delivered payment features in a .NET 10 API and React frontend. The service moved payment workflows out of Core, allowing the team to deploy and evolve them independently.
highlights: Accounting teams and admins can create and edit batches, approve, reject, resubmit, or void payments through a single approval level.
Payment status flows through a third-party payment-automation platform via webhook, with logs available to investigate exceptional cases before updates are returned to Core.
Built LEDES 1998B export templates with the required fields for US legal e-billing.

centerbase.reflection: The durable win was not merely a faster report. It was turning an opaque financial workflow into a clear, maintainable data path that could support the product's next stage of growth.
centerbase.metaDescription: Centerbase case study: redesigned MS SQL accounting reporting across 20+ transaction types, replacing 98 UNION ALL branches and improving report performance by 300%.

toshiba.title: Turning a compressed modernization into a governable delivery.
toshiba.summary: Toshiba Australia needed to modernize an integration-heavy customer portal from Sitecore 8 through 9 to 10 while releasing B2B/B2C capabilities. I combined project-management ownership with senior engineering judgement to keep a fixed-price, high-risk delivery moving.
toshiba.scope: Migration, delivery governance, UAT, release risk

challenge.title: A fixed-price commitment left little room for hidden complexity.
challenge.body: The delivery window was compressed to roughly half of the original technical estimate. At the same time, the platform was not a conventional CMS: it carried B2B/B2C behavior, deep integrations, migration dependencies, uneven local environments, and an expanding team with varied experience.

approach.title: Made technical risk visible early
approach.body: Reviewed migration, compatibility, dependencies, and post-migration structure with Technical Leads. Issues were treated as decisions with owners—not as late surprises during UAT.

approach.title: Turned reporting into an early-warning system
approach.body: Created JQL monitoring views in Confluence for completion, remaining work, defects, blockers, and individual progress; then investigated the root cause and dependency behind every concerning signal.

approach.title: Protected quality while the team scaled
approach.body: Decomposed committed scope into smaller owned workstreams, strengthened QC planning and deployment monitoring, and escalated technical blockers quickly enough to preserve fixed-price milestones.

operatingModel.title: A shared delivery rhythm for a complex release
operatingModel.body: Clear communication channels, two-week planning, twice-weekly customer stand-ups, and visible risk ownership gave the distributed team one operating model from scope to release.

outcome.title: Modernization released with control—not just speed.
outcome.body: Sitecore 10 and the B2B/B2C capabilities went live together. UAT completed on schedule, quality controls helped keep UAT defects comparatively low for the scale, and proactive monitoring surfaced blockers before they grew into schedule failures.
points: Coordinated a Sitecore 8 → 9 → 10 transition and B2B/B2C release.
Supported custom Sitecore libraries where standard platform behavior was insufficient.
Maintained delivery focus through a highly compressed, fixed-price timeline with limited overtime.

toshiba.reflection: In enterprise modernization, alignment is a technical capability. Clear ownership, early risk signals, and credible communication make complex delivery more predictable.
toshiba.metaDescription: Toshiba customer portal case study: technical project leadership for a fixed-price Sitecore 8–10 modernization and B2B/B2C release completed with UAT on schedule.

aspire.eyebrow: Global mobility SaaS · Hands-on technical leadership
aspire.title: Helping a global booking platform move from features to dependable delivery.
aspire.summary: Aspire Lifestyle is an airport-transportation platform operating across more than 16 countries. As Technical Lead, I led the delivery of booking and payment capabilities while evolving the team's architecture, review practice, and sprint discipline.

challenge.title: The work had to expand a reusable platform without losing delivery control.
challenge.body: The customer journey combined airport selection, route discovery, vehicle and journey options, card payment, and operations data. The team needed to respect Aspire's established platform architecture while recovering from Phase 1 instability in scope, quality, demo readiness, and workload balance.

approach.title: Made the booking flow reliable and cost-aware
approach.body: Led the backend journey and Google Maps integration. Address suggestions were delayed until the third typed character, preserving a useful experience while avoiding unnecessary billable autocomplete traffic.

approach.title: Connected payments to operations
approach.body: Designed and integrated Adyen card payments, persisted transaction data, and synchronized payment-status changes from Adyen webhooks. Phase 2 exposed that data in a searchable payment portal for operations staff.

approach.title: Rebuilt the delivery rhythm
approach.body: Identified the map-heavy front-end capability risk, added senior support, and introduced tighter two-week scope control, technical review, workload balancing, release coordination, and client demonstrations.

operatingModel.title: From customer journey to operational confidence
operatingModel.body: The platform connected a customer-facing booking flow to a managed payments workflow—giving both travelers and operations teams a clearer next step.

outcome.title: A stronger platform and a more predictable team.
outcome.body: The team delivered booking and Adyen payment capabilities for a platform operating in 16+ countries. In Phase 2, every deadline was completed without overtime while output quality, scope stability, demo readiness, and customer satisfaction improved.
points: Integrated payment status through persisted transactions and webhook synchronization.
Improved maintainability with shared functions, coding conventions, and technical review.
Balanced hands-on engineering with mentoring, client communication, and release ownership.

aspire.reflection: Technical leadership earned its value here by making delivery calmer: clear standards, the right capability at the right moment, and a rhythm the team could sustain.
aspire.metaDescription: Aspire Lifestyle case study: technical leadership for a global airport booking SaaS across payments, Google Maps integration, and a delivery turnaround serving 16+ countries.
